name: Metasploit Framework
what: An open-source exploitation and post-exploitation framework with modules for reconnaissance, known vulnerability checks, exploits, payloads and pivoting. It is the standard lab platform for proving that a finding is reachable, not only reported by a scanner.
when: In a scoped pentest or purple-team lab when a vulnerability is already triaged and you need a controlled exploit or auxiliary module against systems you are allowed to attack.
cost_note: Metasploit Framework is free and open source; Rapid7 also sells Metasploit Pro with extra UI and automation.
example: Install Framework via the official Rapid7 nightlies or your distro package on an isolated assessment host.
Start `msfconsole`, search for a module that matches a confirmed finding, and set RHOSTS only to in-scope addresses.
Prefer `check` / auxiliary scanners before `exploit`, and capture evidence (session info, proof file) for the report.
Tear down sessions and revert lab snapshots when the test step ends.
pitfalls: Default payloads and meterpreter sessions are noisy and often blocked; agree C2-like traffic with the SOC.
Exploits can crash services; never fire unstable modules at production without a rollback plan.
Keep Framework updated; old modules and stale CVEs waste time and create false confidence.
